properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 7000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to 10 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of up to 3 inches possible down to 6000
feet.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 7000 feet, including Highway 50 and
Interstate 80.

* WHEN...From 8 AM PDT Saturday to 7 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels initially 7000 to 8000 feet
Saturday, lowering to 6000 to 7000 feet Saturday night into Sunday.

flurries possible down to 5000 feet on Saturday night into Sunday,
but no accumulations expected below 6000 feet.

quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
